anti_overlap: Does not review habitus vocabulary bounding, tarpit precedent, or resident-sim's internal autonomy mechanics — that is the generative-agent social-sim reviewer's domain
Does not review replay-hash canonicalization, save/schema compatibility, or trace-possession merge semantics — that is the deterministic-simulation/replay-engineering reviewer's domain
Evaluates era handling and federation only from the player-facing product/rendering angle; the underlying schema/provenance compatibility question belongs to the replay-engineering reviewer
decision_lens: Score P0 when a claim of mode independence or enforceable product structure (decision 11, §6) is contradicted by a mechanical requirement elsewhere in the design (e.g. Legacy Mode's manual file-level exchange, decision 6) such that the promised experience cannot occur for the majority of plausible players. Score P1 when a cross-layer content contract (era handling / lossy misreading, decision 8) is specified at the data-schema level but has no rendering/consumption design at the player-facing layer, making the guardrail unimplementable rather than merely unspecified. Score P2 when a sequencing decision (R7 federation deferral) is undermined by v1 already paying that decision's engineering cost without its payoff, which wastes effort without breaking anything today. Score P3 for naming/framing polish.
focus: Whether the async-mode join actually delivers 'one game, two modes' as a playable, enforceable product — independent-playability under §6, era-mismatch handling as something a player experiences rather than a data-layer abstraction, and whether v1's file-level own-runs join is doing federation's hard work early without federation's payoff.
name: fd-gamedesign-async-trace-exchange
persona: Apply the perspective of an asynchronous-multiplayer and live-service game designer steeped in the genre this join explicitly cites — Elden Ring's message/bloodstain/invasion traces, Dragon's Dogma's pawn-rental economy, Death Stranding's structure-sharing, Journey's anonymous-stranger design — someone who evaluates every 'players don't need each other but the game is richer when they overlap' pitch by asking what actually renders on screen for the player who never touches the other half.
review_areas: Independent-playability vs the mechanics of the join — decision 11 and §6 promise 'no game blocks on the universe' and modes ship independently playable, but decision 6's own-runs Legacy Mode (file-level, no backend) requires a player to own both games and manually move an export between them; assess what fraction of the promised 'duality' fiction (being-seen / seeing) actually fires for a player who owns only one game, and whether that's the intended 'garnish until it isn't' state or an unstated failure mode

Era-mismatch as rendered content, not just as a data contract — decision 8 states Now-era traces reach far-era ravenous runs only as 'oldest-stratum records' via §5.3's lossy-misreading budget, borrowed from a context (shadow-work chronicle → ER worldgen text) where the consumer is procedural myth generation, not a live player-controlled witness channel; determine whether the design specifies what a player actually sees/experiences when a mismatched-era trace surfaces in ravenous's witness channel, or whether this is asserted at the schema level with no player-facing design

R7 federation deferral vs v1's actual engineering surface — v1's own-runs join already requires a trace file format one engine build's export can be read by (eventually) another, which is federation's hard problem (cross-version, cross-instance schema compatibility); assess whether v1 is quietly doing federation's expensive part (a stable cross-producer file format) without federation's stated payoff (a shared pawn pool), and whether that's deliberate de-risking or scope-creep mislabeled as deferral

The fiction-to-mechanism mapping ('being seen' / 'seeing') — evaluate whether the stated duality (fashionsomething's core verb is being seen, ravenous's core channel is seeing) actually maps onto CommuteResult v2's event log and ravenous's witness channel as designed, or whether the fiction is aspirational framing sitting on top of a mechanism (file-level trace import) that doesn't structurally deliver 'being seen' by another live player in v1 (only by one's own past runs)

Load-bearing ordering of the open questions from a product-sequencing lens — assess whether Q6 (do ravens appear in fashionsomething as return-direction live trace) and Q8 (does fashionsomething-dk4 absorb CommuteResult v2 work) are actually prerequisite product decisions that the current Key Decisions section implicitly assumes answers to, rather than independent open items

What's missing: absence of any player-facing failure/degenerate-case design — no discussion of what a ward looks like with zero traces ever imported (the everyday case for most of a game's life, per decision 1's Dragon's Dogma degradation-floor framing, which is stated for the AI-pawn-pool half but not verified against actual expected trace-import rates)

severity_examples.condition: No mechanism gets the join's fiction to fire for a single-game-owning player, and the design doesn't acknowledge this as the default case.
severity_examples.scenario: Decision 11 and §6 both promise mode independence ('no game blocks on the universe,' 'ships independently playable'), but decision 6's join mechanism (own-runs Legacy Mode, file-level, no backend) means the join's entire headline fiction — fashionsomething's being-seen paired with ravenous's seeing — requires a single player to own both games and manually export/import a file; for any player who owns only one game (the majority, by ordinary attach-rate expectations), the promised duality never fires at all, which is a different and unaddressed failure mode from the design's own framing of 'traces are garnish until they aren't.'

severity_examples.condition: No player-facing rendering or consumption design exists for era-mismatched trace records inside ravenous's witness channel.
severity_examples.scenario: Era handling (decision 8) states Now-era traces reach far-era ravenous runs only as 'oldest-stratum records, never live street state,' citing §5.3's lossy-misreading budget — but that budget (Engramicon v0's fidelity_ceiling/floor/anchors) was designed for a producer that generates procedural myth TEXT for worldgen, not for a live witness channel a human plays through; the brainstorm never specifies what actually renders in ravenous when an era-mismatched trace surfaces (an NPC? a myth-fragment UI element? nothing at all?), making the guardrail a data-layer assertion with no implementation path at the player-facing layer.

severity_examples.condition: v1's trace file format is not evaluated against whether it's doing federation-grade work ahead of federation's scheduled payoff.
severity_examples.scenario: fashionsomething's R7 defers cross-player federation 'much later,' but v1's own-runs join already commits to a cross-producer, cross-engine-version trace file format (Engramicon-v0-aligned, decision 5) — the exact artifact federation would need to build the real pawn pool; the design doesn't check whether v1 is already spending federation's format-design cost without federation's shared-pool payoff, which either de-risks federation cheaply (good) or represents scope paid early for no v1 benefit (waste) — the brainstorm doesn't say which was intended.
